references.text: Makir, son of Manasseh, is mentioned as the patriarch. Joseph saw Ephraim's descendants to the third generation, and the children of Makir, son of Manasseh, were born on his knees.
The daughters of Zelophehad were descendants of Makir and Gilead from the tribe of Manasseh, confirming the lineage.
Makir's sons went to Gilead and captured it. Moses gave Gilead to Makir, son of Manasseh.
The family heads from the clan of Gilead, son of Makir, son of Manasseh, came forward with a case concerning inheritance.
Gilead was given to Makir as an inheritance on the east side of the Jordan.
Makir was the firstborn of Manasseh and father of Gilead. Makir received Gilead and Bashan because he was a warrior.
Half of Gilead was given to Makir's descendants.
The genealogy of Manasseh through Makir and Gilead is confirmed, with details about their settlements.
Manasseh's descendants through Makir and Gilead are listed along with their families.
